patients.summary: 56-year-old school district administrative coordinator with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity and symptomatic gallstones who joined in 2024. Cholangitis from a common duct stone in December 2025, interval cholecystectomy in February 2026 complicated by vagal bradycardia on insufflation and post-intubation laryngitis, then a retained duct stone with cholangitis and septic shock in March 2026. Recovered and back to routine care.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

54F here to establish. Prior PCP retired; records requested. Works as an administrative coordinator for the school district, so the first weeks of September are busy for her.

Diabetes: type 2 since 2018. Metformin 1000 BID and glipizide 5 qAM. Checks sugars a few mornings a week and says they run about where her old doctor wanted. No lows. No numbness or burning in the feet. Eye exam last year with an optometrist, told no diabetic changes.

HTN: on lisinopril 10 for years. Home cuff readings at goal by her report. No cough.

Gallstones: found on an ultrasound last year after a few attacks of RUQ/epigastric pain. Gets an episode every few months, usually after a heavy or fried meal: steady ache under the right ribs, sometimes into the back, lasts a couple of hours, then settles. Last one in July. Never had fever, yellow eyes or dark urine with them. Prior PCP talked about seeing a surgeon. She knows her mother and sister both had gallbladder trouble.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, obesity, cholelithiasis.
PSH: T&A as a child (1978), C-section 1994.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother T2DM and gallstones (gallbladder out at 52); father HTN and high cholesterol; older sister gallstones.
SHx: former smoker, roughly 8 pack-years, quit 2015. Wine 1-2 glasses on weekends. No drugs. Walks some evenings.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, edema. No change in bowels. No urinary symptoms. Mood good.

EXAM: well appearing, pleasant. See vitals. BMI 33.
HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement.
Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abd obese, soft, nontender today, no organomegaly, low transverse scar well healed.
Ext no edema. Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP and PT pulses 2+.
Skin no rash. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2: 0.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN
1. T2DM - on metformin/glipizide. A1c today. Reviewed hypoglycemia rules with glipizide (don't skip meals, carry glucose tabs). Urine microalbumin today. Eye exam due this fall, she will book with her optometrist.
2. HTN - at goal in office and at home. Continue lisinopril 10. CMP today.
3. Obesity - BMI 33. Talked about walking more regularly; she is open to it once the school year settles.
4. Cholelithiasis with recurrent biliary colic - symptomatic stones, discussed that elective cholecystectomy is the usual answer and offered a general surgery referral. She'd rather not take time off right now and wants to think it over. Reviewed red flags: pain lasting more than a few hours, fever, yellowing, dark urine - go to the ED. Lower-fat meals may cut down on attacks.
5. Lipids - continue atorvastatin 20. Lipid panel today.
6. Health maintenance - flu shot today. Hep C and HIV screening today (never done). Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy, Pap and vaccine history from old records when they arrive. Shingrix and COVID booster discussed for next month.

RTC 3 months for diabetes, sooner prn.

No changes to your medications. We'll recheck the A1c in December.

Good to meet you, and good luck with the start of the year at the district.

documents.title: Gallbladder again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. Just letting you know I had another gallbladder attack Saturday night after we went out to dinner (I had the fish and chips, I know). Same pain under my right ribs going around to my back, lasted about 3 hours and then went away on its own. No fever and my eyes weren't yellow. I'm fine now and ate normally yesterday. Should I be doing anything?

documents.title: RE: Gallbladder again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sandra, thanks for letting me know, and glad it settled. That sounds like the same biliary colic you've had before. Since these keep coming back, I'd still recommend seeing a general surgeon about taking the gallbladder out - I'm happy to put in the referral whenever you say the word. If pain goes longer than 4-5 hours, or you get fever, chills, yellow skin or eyes, or dark urine, go to the ED rather than waiting it out. We can talk more at your visit next week.

documents.title: RE: RE: Gallbladder again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. I really can't be out for surgery before the school year is over. Can I call you in June about the referral?

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 12/01/2025

CC: Right-sided abdominal pain, fever, yellow eyes.

HPI: 55-year-old woman with known gallstones, type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Two days of constant pain under the right ribs, worse than her usual attacks and not letting up. Fevers and chills since yesterday. Noticed her eyes looked yellow this morning. Slow to answer and unsure of the date; history partly limited by her confusion.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, obesity, cholelithiasis with prior biliary colic.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Temp 38.9 C (102 F), BP 90/60, HR 110. Ill appearing, scleral icterus, disoriented to date. Abdomen: RUQ tenderness, no rebound, no guarding. Lungs clear. No rash.

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.5, plt 250. Na 136, Cl 100, HCO3 16, anion gap 20, BUN 18, Cr 1.0. T bili 3.0 / direct 2.5, AST 80, ALT 75, alk phos 300. Lactate 4.5. Blood cultures x2 sent.
Bedside and formal RUQ US: dilated CBD with a distal stone; gallstones.

ED course: IV crystalloid bolus, with blood pressure and mentation improving. IV piperacillin-tazobactam after cultures. GI paged for ERCP.

Impression: acute cholangitis from choledocholithiasis.
Disposition: admitted to hospital medicine.

documents.title: ERCP Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY
Date of procedure: 12/02/2025
Indication: acute cholangitis, distal CBD stone on ultrasound.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.

The duodenoscope was passed to the second portion of the duodenum. The major papilla appeared normal. Deep biliary cannulation achieved. Cholangiogram showed a dilated common bile duct with a filling defect in the distal duct. Biliary sphincterotomy was performed. The stone was extracted with balloon sweeps, followed by purulent bile. Final occlusion cholangiogram showed no remaining filling defects. The pancreatic duct was not injected.

Impression: choledocholithiasis, cleared after sphincterotomy and balloon extraction.
Recommendations: continue antibiotics; general surgery referral for cholecystectomy in the coming weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/01/2025, discharged 12/05/2025.

Diagnosis: acute cholangitis due to choledocholithiasis. Cholelithiasis.

Course: Presented with RUQ pain, fever, jaundice and confusion; hypotension and lactate 4.5 corrected with IV fluids in the ED and she did not need pressors or ICU care. Started on IV piperacillin-tazobactam. ERCP 12/02 with sphincterotomy and stone extraction, duct clear. Fever resolved by hospital day 2, confusion cleared within the first day, and bilirubin and liver enzymes trended down daily. Blood cultures no growth. Metformin and glipizide held while inpatient with correctional insulin; restarted on discharge with normal kidney function and good intake.

Discharge meds: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID through 12/08 (7 days total antibiotics). Resume metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily (blood pressure normal by discharge), atorvastatin 20 mg qHS.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with liver tests and CBC. General surgery clinic for interval cholecystectomy - appointment made for 12/22. Return for fever, pain or yellowing.

documents.title: Transition of Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 business days after discharge (hospital records received 12/8). Feels "wiped out but so much better." No fever since the hospital. Pain gone. Eyes back to white. Eating small low-fat meals. Finished the last antibiotic dose last night. Back on all home meds as listed in the summary; fasting sugars a bit up the first day home, now back to her usual. Surgery appointment 12/22. Booked TCM visit with PCP 12/11 with labs. Knows to go to the ED for fever, pain or jaundice.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Discharge summary, ED record and ERCP report reviewed.

Admitted 12/1-12/5 with acute cholangitis from a distal common duct stone; ERCP 12/2 with sphincterotomy and clearance. Fluids and IV antibiotics, never needed the ICU. Finished amoxicillin-clavulanate 12/8.

Today: energy coming back, back at work half days this week. No pain, fever, chills. Stools and urine normal color. Eating low-fat. Sugars back to usual. Remembers little of the first evening in the ED.

Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 5, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 20. Antibiotic course complete.

Exam: looks well. Afebrile. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild residual RUQ discomfort on deep palpation only, no guarding. No edema.

A/P
1. Choledocholithiasis with cholangitis - treated, duct cleared, clinically resolved. Liver tests and CBC today to confirm the trend.
2. Cholelithiasis - gallbladder still in with stones; she is now very motivated. Surgery consult 12/22 for interval cholecystectomy. Will need preop eval - book once surgery date is set.
3. T2DM/HTN - back on usual regimen, BP fine today.
Call or go to ED for fever, pain or jaundice before surgery.

documents.title: General Surgery Consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
GENERAL SURGERY CLINIC - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 12/22/2025
Re: Sandra Wojcik, DOB 07/20/1970

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Wojcik after her admission earlier this month for acute cholangitis due to choledocholithiasis, treated with ERCP, sphincterotomy and stone extraction on 12/2. She has had gallstones on imaging since 2023 with intermittent biliary colic, and her mother and sister both had gallbladder disease.

She is pain free today and has completed antibiotics. Medical history: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity. Prior C-section and tonsillectomy. Medications: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA. Former smoker.

Exam: well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed low transverse incision.

Assessment: symptomatic cholelithiasis after choledocholithiasis with cholangitis. Interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy is recommended to prevent recurrence. We discussed risks including bleeding, infection, bile leak, bile duct injury, conversion to open and the small chance of a further duct stone.

Plan: laparoscopic cholecystectomy scheduled 02/06/2026. Please complete a preoperative evaluation including a 12-lead ECG given her diabetes and hypertension, and send it to our office. Hold metformin, glipizide and lisinopril the morning of surgery.

Sincerely,
General Surgery

PREOPERATIVE MEDICAL EVALUATION
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 2/6/2026, general surgery. General anesthesia planned.

History: cholangitis from a common duct stone 12/2025 treated with ERCP, sphincterotomy and extraction; long history of gallstones with colic. No pain since discharge. T2DM on metformin and glipizide, HTN on lisinopril, obesity, on atorvastatin.
Prior anesthesia: T&A as a child, C-section 1994 - no problems she knows of. No family history of anesthesia reactions.
Functional capacity: walks 30 min, climbs 2 flights without stopping, well over 4 METs. No chest pain, dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations or syncope. No snoring or daytime sleepiness she has noticed.
NKDA. Former smoker.

Exam: vitals as charted. Airway: normal mouth opening, neck full range. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

ECG today: normal sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no conduction abnormality.

Assessment: low risk for a low-risk procedure. No further cardiac testing needed. Medically optimized.

Periop plan:
- Metformin: hold the morning of surgery, resume when eating.
- Glipizide: hold the morning of surgery, resume when eating normally.
- Lisinopril: hold the morning of surgery, resume the next day if BP allows.
- Atorvastatin: continue.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 02/06/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: symptomatic cholelithiasis, status post ERCP for choledocholithiasis with cholangitis.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
EBL: minimal. Specimen: gallbladder to pathology. Complications: intraoperative bradycardia with insufflation, resolved (see below).

Description: After induction and intubation the abdomen was prepped and draped. Periumbilical access with a Hasson technique, CO2 pneumoperitoneum established, three additional ports placed under direct vision. About thirty minutes into the case, during insufflation, anesthesia called a sudden fall in heart rate to 40 with blood pressure 110/70; she was otherwise stable and there had been no technical difficulty. The abdomen was desufflated and atropine 0.5 mg IV given by anesthesia, with heart rate recovering to the 70s within about a minute. After a brief pause, pneumoperitoneum was re-established slowly at a lower pressure without recurrence. The gallbladder was retracted, the critical view of safety obtained, and the cystic duct and artery clipped and divided. The gallbladder was removed from the liver bed with cautery and extracted in a bag. Hemostasis confirmed. Ports removed under vision, fascia closed at the umbilicus, skin closed with absorbable suture.

Impression: uncomplicated laparoscopic cholecystectomy apart from vagal bradycardia from the pneumoperitoneum, which responded promptly.
Plan: overnight observation on telemetry given the intraoperative bradycardia.

documents.title: Surgical Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
SHORT STAY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/06/2026 for laparoscopic cholecystectomy; discharged 02/07/2026.

Intraoperative vagal bradycardia during CO2 insufflation, treated with desufflation and atropine; procedure completed. Preoperative ECG had been normal sinus rhythm. Overnight telemetry: sinus rhythm throughout, no further bradycardia. Tolerated diet, ambulating, pain controlled with oral medicines. Sore throat from the breathing tube noted on the morning of discharge.

Discharge medications: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 mg 1 tab q6h prn severe pain, #10; acetaminophen 1000 mg q8h prn (do not combine above 3 g/day total acetaminophen). Resume metformin, glipizide, lisinopril and atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic in 2 weeks. Pathology pending at discharge.

documents.title: Office Visit - Hoarseness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6 days s/p lap chole (2/6, general ET anesthesia). Op note and discharge summary reviewed: bradycardia to 40 with insufflation, reversed with desufflation and atropine, case completed, no recurrence overnight on tele.

Hoarse since extubation with a raw throat. Not worse, not better. Swallowing solids and liquids fine. No stridor, dyspnea, cough, fever. No palpitations, lightheadedness or fainting since surgery. Incisions sore but OK. Off the oxycodone, using acetaminophen once a day.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Voice hoarse, breathy. Oropharynx without exudate. No neck swelling or tenderness, no nodes. No stridor. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Port sites clean, dry, no erythema.

A/P
1. Acute laryngitis - post-intubation. Voice rest (no whispering), humidifier, fluids, avoid throat clearing. Should settle over 1-2 weeks. If still hoarse at 3 weeks, call and we'll get ENT to look.
2. Vagal bradycardia from pneumoperitoneum - single intraoperative event, normal preop ECG, no symptoms since; resolved, nothing further needed.
3. Post-op - healing well, surgery f/u 2/20.
Work note given for 2 days of reduced phone duties.

documents.title: General Surgery Postoperative Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Ms. Wojcik was seen on 02/20/2026, two weeks after her laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She is eating a normal diet without pain, bowels are regular, and she has no fever. Her voice is improving. Port sites are healed with no hernia or infection.

Pathology showed gallstones without dysplasia or malignancy, which we reviewed with her.

She may return to all activity. No routine surgical follow-up is needed; we would be glad to see her again if any problem arises. Medications unchanged: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA.

Thank you for referring her.

General Surgery

documents.title: Voice is back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to say my voice is completely back to normal as of this week. Thanks for seeing me so quickly. Surgeon released me last Friday too.

documents.title: RE: Voice is back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news, Sandra. Glad you're through all of it. See you in May for your diabetes check, or sooner if needed.

conditions.note: Retained common bile duct stone after cholecystectomy

medications.reason: Held at hospital discharge after septic shock

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food through 03/16 to complete the antibiotic course

results.text: No growth at 5 days (2 of 2 sets)

reports.text:
ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND (EMERGENCY)
Indication: RUQ pain, fever, jaundice; cholecystectomy one month ago.
Comparison: RUQ ultrasound 12/01/2025.
Findings: The gallbladder is surgically absent; no fluid collection in the gallbladder fossa. Echogenic shadowing stone in the common bile duct with dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts. Liver normal in echotexture without focal lesion. Visualized pancreas unremarkable. Kidneys without hydronephrosis. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Common bile duct stone with intrahepatic biliary dilation. Status post cholecystectomy.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 03/07/2026 (Saturday)

CC: Severe right upper abdominal pain, fever, yellow skin.

HPI: 55F, laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2/6/2026, ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone removal 12/2025 for cholangitis, T2DM, HTN. Since last night: severe RUQ pain, fevers, nausea and several episodes of vomiting, yellow skin this morning. Over the past hour in the department she has become more confused and drowsy.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 22. Jaundiced, in obvious distress, drowsy and intermittently confused. Marked RUQ tenderness. Port sites healed. Lungs clear.

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.5, plt 250. T bili 5.2, direct 3.8, alk phos 210, AST 80, ALT 75. Amylase 300, lipase 900. Blood cultures x2.
Ultrasound: CBD stone with intrahepatic ductal dilation; gallbladder absent.

Course: IV fluid boluses with BP persistently low; norepinephrine started. IV piperacillin-tazobactam after cultures. Critical care and GI consulted.

Impression: recurrent choledocholithiasis with acute cholangitis; septic shock.
Disposition: ICU.

documents.title: ERCP Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY
Date of procedure: 03/08/2026, ICU patient, performed under general anesthesia.
Indication: cholangitis with septic shock; CBD stone on ultrasound; prior sphincterotomy 12/2025; cholecystectomy 2/2026.

Prior sphincterotomy noted and patent. Deep biliary cannulation. Cholangiogram: dilated common bile duct with a single filling defect in the distal duct and dilated intrahepatic ducts. Cystic duct stump clips in good position, no leak. Balloon sweeps removed one stone with sludge and purulent bile. Occlusion cholangiogram: no residual filling defects, good drainage.

Impression: retained/recurrent common bile duct stone, cleared.
Recommendations: complete antibiotics; GI clinic follow-up in about 6 weeks with liver tests.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/07/2026 (ICU 03/07-03/10), discharged 03/13/2026.

Diagnoses: septic shock due to acute cholangitis; recurrent choledocholithiasis (retained common duct stone) one month after cholecystectomy. Amylase and lipase elevation on arrival with the stone impacted in the distal duct, trending down after drainage.

Course: Hypotensive despite fluid resuscitation; norepinephrine for about 24 hours in the ICU. IV piperacillin-tazobactam. ERCP 03/08 with balloon extraction of a distal duct stone; duct clear. Off norepinephrine 03/09, mentation back to baseline the same day. Transferred to the floor 03/10. Bilirubin, liver enzymes and lipase falling daily; tolerating a low-fat diet. Blood cultures without growth. Metformin and glipizide held in the ICU with insulin; resumed 03/12 when eating normally and kidney function normal.

Discharge medications:
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID through 03/16 to complete the course.
- Metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS - continue.
- Lisinopril 10 mg - HOLD until seen by PCP, given recent shock; blood pressure normal off it in hospital.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week (liver tests, CBC, BMP, lipase, BP check and decision on lisinopril). GI clinic in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Transition of Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital records received this morning, reviewed. Called pt. Home since Friday. Very tired, sleeping a lot, appetite slowly coming back. No fever, no pain, color normal. Last antibiotic dose tonight. Not taking lisinopril per hospital instructions; taking metformin, glipizide, atorvastatin. Fasting sugars ok, no lows. Has a home cuff - asked her to check BP daily and bring the readings. Booked with PCP Thu 3/19, labs same day. District has her out through next week. ED for fever, pain, jaundice or confusion.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up, high complexity. ED record, ERCP report and discharge summary reviewed.

Summary: 3/7-3/13 admission (ICU 3 days) for septic shock from acute cholangitis due to a retained common duct stone, a month after lap chole. Needed norepinephrine about a day. ERCP 3/8 with balloon extraction, duct clear. Lipase was 900 on arrival with the stone at the ampulla, falling with drainage. Cultures negative. Finished amox-clav 3/16.

Now: tired but improving each day, walking around the block. No pain, fever, chills, vomiting. Eating small meals. Urine and stool normal color. Thinking clear - remembers almost nothing of the first day. Home BP readings since discharge running higher than her usual. Sugars fine.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 5, atorvastatin 20. Lisinopril on hold since discharge.

Exam: tired-appearing but well. Afebrile. BP as charted, above goal. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, port sites healed. No edema. Alert, oriented, conversing normally.

A/P
1. Septic shock from cholangitis - resolved. Off pressors since 3/9, antibiotics complete.
2. Choledocholithiasis with cholangitis (retained stone) - cleared at ERCP, clinically resolved. Repeat LFTs, lipase, CBC today. GI clinic 4/21.
3. HTN - BP back up off lisinopril, kidney function normal at discharge. Restart lisinopril 10 daily; BMP today and keep home log.
4. T2DM - back on metformin/glipizide, no lows; A1c at May visit.
She asked whether this could happen again - explained a further duct stone is possible but much less likely now that the gallbladder is out and the duct has been cleared twice; warning signs reviewed. Return to work note for 3/30.

documents.title: Hospital follow-up labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sandra - good news. Your liver tests, lipase and white count are all back to normal, and your kidney function and potassium are fine, so it's safe to be back on the lisinopril. Keep checking your blood pressure at home and send me a few readings in a couple of weeks. Rest up.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Clinic Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CLINIC
Date of visit: 04/21/2026

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Wojcik in follow-up after her ERCP of 03/08/2026, when a retained distal common bile duct stone was cleared during an admission for cholangitis with septic shock. This followed an earlier ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction in 12/2025 and laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 02/2026.

She has been well since discharge with no abdominal pain, fever, jaundice, nausea or change in stool or urine color. She is back at work full time.

Medications: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA.
Exam: well appearing, anicteric. Abdomen soft and nontender.

Liver tests drawn today are normal.

Impression: choledocholithiasis, cleared, now status post cholecystectomy with a patent sphincterotomy.
Plan: no further ERCP or imaging planned. She knows to seek care urgently for pain, fever or jaundice, and we would be happy to see her again if symptoms recur.

Sincerely,
Gastroenterology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: DM/HTN f/u, first routine visit since the March admission. Feels like herself again, back to evening walks. No abdominal pain, fever or jaundice. GI letter 4/21: LFTs normal, no further ERCP planned. Back on lisinopril since 3/19 - home BPs back to her usual range. Sugars stable, no lows. Taking all meds.

O: vitals as charted. Well. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Feet: intact skin, sensation normal, pulses good. No edema.

A/P
1. T2DM - A1c and BMP today. Continue metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 5.
2. HTN - back at goal on lisinopril 10.
3. S/p cholecystectomy, choledocholithiasis x2 cleared - doing well, nothing further.
4. Lipids - atorvastatin 20, lipids with the fall physical.
RTC September for physical; flu/COVID then.

documents.title: May labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sandra, your A1c is 7.6 - better than January, though still a little above where you usually run. After the winter you've had I'm comfortable leaving your medicines as they are and rechecking at your physical. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the lisinopril. See you in September.

documents.title: 90-Day Supply Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order renewal request: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS, 90-day supplies. Lisinopril restarted 3/19 at the same dose. Last visit 5/19. Pended to PCP - approved, 3 refills each.

documents.title: Physical appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, I'd like to book my yearly physical for after school starts, ideally a Tuesday early morning. Can I get my flu shot at the same time?

documents.title: RE: Physical appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Sandra, you're booked Tuesday 9/22 at 7:40 AM. Please come fasting for labs. Flu vaccine should be in by then and we can give it at the visit.
